standard.title: Arts importance for communities
standard.description: explore how and why the arts are important for people and communities
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior knowledge assumed. Students bring awareness of arts experiences from family and community life.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how and why the arts — including dance — are important for people and communities.

nodes.label: Recognising arts in everyday life
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify arts works and experiences — including dances and songs — that are present in their own lives and communities.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying at least one type of arts work or experience from their own life — songs they sing, dances they watch or perform, animations, community events.
nodes.typical_width: Identifying a range of arts experiences across multiple forms — songs for celebrations, dances, public art, digital works — and sharing ideas and feelings about these with peers and teachers.
wider: Listen to First Nations Australians talk about the importance of arts for connecting to People, Culture and Country/Place (using resources created or co-created by First Nations Australians)
Explore dances or songs from students' cultural communities — identifying what they are used for and who participates
nodes.hinge_reason: Without recognising arts as present and purposeful in their own lives, students lack a reference point for understanding arts as communicative and culturally meaningful — the conceptual grounding for N2.

response_modes.reason: Students from different cultural backgrounds have access to different arts experiences. Sharing across the class builds collective recognition of arts' diversity and omnipresence.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Identifying a rich range of arts experiences — across cultures and forms — builds a broad, genuine understanding of arts as a community practice rather than a school activity.
success_criteria: Student can name at least one arts experience from their own life
Student can share an idea or feeling about an arts work they have experienced

nodes.label: Understanding arts communicate emotion and ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe how facial expressions, gestures, movement and voice in arts works communicate emotions and feelings.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying how a character or performer in a simple arts work (cartoon, song, dance) communicates an emotion through their face, voice or movement.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring how facial expressions, gestures, movement and voice communicate emotions and feelings across a range of arts forms — portraits, cartoons, songs, chants, dances from different times and cultures.
wider: Explore how illustrations and images in picture books communicate mood, character, and narrative without words
Compare how the same emotion (e.g. joy, sadness) is communicated differently across two different arts forms or cultural contexts

response_modes.reason: Students need language and observational frames to read arts works — prompt with 'How do you know they are happy/sad?', 'What does the dancer do to show that?'. Viewpoints-style questions scaffold the looking.

success_criteria: Student can identify an emotion being communicated in a simple arts work
Student can point to at least one feature (face, movement, voice) that communicates that emotion

nodes.label: Arts bring people together
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that arts experiences — including dances, songs and celebrations — bring people together and have meaning for communities.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying at least one arts experience that brings people together — a school song, a celebration dance, a community performance.
nodes.typical_width: Identifying social and cultural dances, songs and performances that have meaning for communities — including celebrations, ceremonies and shared cultural practices — and sharing observations about who participates and why.
wider: Learn a social or cultural dance that has meaning for a specific community, observing relevant protocols
Explore First Nations Australian dances used in ceremonies or community events — discussing how they connect people to Culture and Country/Place

response_modes.reason: Students understand 'community' most concretely when exploring arts practices from communities they recognise — their own family traditions, school events, local events. Broadening context builds genuine understanding.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who encounter arts practices from multiple cultural communities develop a rich, non-tokenistic understanding of arts as community knowledge — a foundation for respectful engagement with First Nations arts throughout F-10.
success_criteria: Student can name or describe an arts experience that brings people together
Student can say something about why the arts experience is meaningful for the people involved
